arxiv-2108-04628.title: Learning Canonical 3D Object Representation for Fine-Grained Recognition Thanks: This work was supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) grant funded by the Korea government (MSIP) (NRF-2021R1A2C2006703), and the Yonsei University Research Fund of 2021 (2021-22-0001).
arxiv-2108-04628.creator: Sunghun Joung, Seungryong Kim, Minsu Kim, Ig-Jae Kim, Kwanghoon Sohn
arxiv-2108-04628.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sunghun Joung, Seungryong Kim, Minsu Kim, Ig-Jae Kim, Kwanghoon Sohn. We propose a novel framework for fine-grained object recognition that learns to recover object variation in 3D space from a single image, trained on an image collection without using any ground-truth 3D annotation. We accomplish this by representing an object as a composition of 3D shape and its appearance, while eliminating the effect of camera viewpoint, in a canonical configuration.

arxiv-2312-03271.title: Freezing of sessile droplet and frost halo formation
arxiv-2312-03271.creator: Sivanandan Kavuri 1 , George Karapetsas 2 , Chander Shekhar Sharma 3 and Kirti Chandra Sahu 1
arxiv-2312-03271.description: Abstract The freezing of a sessile droplet unveils fascinating physics, characterised by the emergence of a frost halo on the underlying substrate, the progression of the liquid-ice interface, and the formation of a cusp-like morphology at the tip of the droplet.

arxiv-2401-16322.title: High-order exponential integration for seismic wave modeling Fernando V. Ravelo (ORCID: 0000-0003-1867-2123) Martin Schreiber (ORCID: 0000-0002-4430-6779) Pedro S. Peixoto (ORCID: 0000-0003-2358-3221)
arxiv-2401-16322.creator: Fernando V. Ravelo, Martin Schreiber, Pedro S. Peixoto
arxiv-2401-16322.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Fernando V. Ravelo, Martin Schreiber, Pedro S. Peixoto. Seismic imaging is a major challenge in geophysics with broad applications. It involves solving wave propagation equations with absorbing boundary conditions (ABC) multiple times. This drives the need for accurate and efficient numerical methods. This study examines a collection of exponential integration methods, known for their good numerical properties on wave representation, to investigate their efficacy in solving the wave equation with ABC. The purpose of this research is to assess the performance of these methods.

arxiv-2410-02884.creator: Di Zhang, Jianbo Wu, Jingdi Lei, Tong Che, Jiatong Li, Tong Xie, Xiaoshui Huang, Shufei Zhang, Marco Pavone, Yuqiang Li , Wanli Ouyang, Dongzhan Zhou
arxiv-2410-02884.description: Abstract This paper presents an advanced mathematical reasoning framework, LLaMA-Berry , for enhancing the problem-solving ability of large language models (LLMs). pmc-12374108.title: Analysis of the Distribution of Private Research Funding to Sports Medicine Orthopaedic Surgeons
pmc-12374108.creator: Aakash K. Shah, Isha K. Shah, Robert J. Burkhart, Heath P. Gould, Jacob G. Calcei, Sabrina M. Strickland, James E. Voos
pmc-12374108.description: Background:The Physician Payments Sunshine Act mandated the public reporting of all industry payments above a $10 value that are disbursed to physicians in the United States. pmc-12501029.creator: Andreas Holmqvist, Nur Mehpare Kocaturk, Christina Duncan, Jennifer Riley, Steven Baginski, Graham Marsh, Joel Cresser-Brown, Hannah Maple, Kristiina Juvonen, Gajanan Sathe, Nicola Morrice, Calum Sutherland, Kevin D Read, William Farnaby
pmc-12501029.description: Bifunctional targeted protein degraders, also known as Proteolysis Targeting Chimeras (PROTACs), are an emerging drug modality that may offer a new approach for treating neurodegenerative diseases. Identifying chemical starting points for PROTACs remains a largely empirical process and the design rules for identifying Central Nervous System (CNS) active PROTACs have yet to be established.

pmc-13473299.title: The Impact of Visible Symptoms of Thallus Damage on the Phycobiota of Mediterranean Epiphytic Lichens
pmc-13473299.creator: Tamara Pazos, Patricia Moya, Salvador Chiva, Pavel Škaloud, Veronika Kantnerová, Eva Barreno, Isaac Garrido-Benavent
pmc-13473299.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Lichens are excellent bioindicators of overall ecosystem health. The symbiotic nature of their thalli enables tracking changes in humidity, temperature, habitat disturbance and air pollution, often before larger plants do. Sensitive species usually show visible thallus damage, such as bleaching or changes in colour (including total or partial necrosis, and death of the photosynthetic component of the symbiosis), slow growth, and/or biases in reproductive strategies.

pmc-13550570.title: Entrepreneurship education shapes creativity among Egyptian hospitality students through entrepreneurial attitudes and intentions
pmc-13550570.creator: Omar Alsetoohy, Mahmoud Abou Kamar, Ahmad Samed Al-Adwan, Sayed M. Ismail, Anwar Hammad Al-Rashidi, Khaled Ahmed Abdel-Al Ibrahim
pmc-13550570.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study developed and tested a psychological model explaining associations between entrepreneurship education (EE) and student creativity and entrepreneurial behavior, drawing on the theory of planned behavior (TPB) and the componential theory of creativity (CTC). Using a cross-sectional survey of 335 hospitality students and analyzing the data with partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), the study examined the relationships of EE with individual creativity, university-level creativity, entrepreneurial attitudes, and entrepreneurial intentions.

pmc-13569563.title: Time for a Change: Why Psycholinguistics Should Move Beyond the Content-Function Word Distinction
pmc-13569563.creator: Solvej Wilbrandt Jaeger, Kasper Boye
pmc-13569563.description: The traditional distinction between content and function words continues to underpin much psycholinguistic research, even though other areas of linguistics have long recognized it as problematic (e.g. Bennis et al., 1983, and Ishkhanyan et al., 2017 within aphasiology; Diessel, 1999: 150–153, and Bisang, 2010: 291 within linguistic typology; Emonds, 1985: 162–164, and Rauh, 1993 within grammatical theory).

pmc-13679026.description: IntroductionCerebrospinal meningitis is a clinical syndrome with multiple etiologies, however, in sub-Saharan Africa, infectious and contagious forms remain highly prevalent and carry high risks of mortality and disability. The Upper West Region of Ghana is found within the meningitis belt and frequently records the highest numbers of incident meningitis cases within the country yearly.
